GOAL: ready-to-integrate Docker recipes to add **Satisfactory** and **Terraria** as Dockerized game servers on Nxeon.

Nxeon runs each game as a Docker container via a community image, installed by a one-line setupScript. EXACT existing pattern:
- Minecraft: `curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com | sh && docker run -d --name mc -e EULA=TRUE -e MEMORY=2G -p 25565:25565 -v /opt/mc:/data --restart unless-stopped itzg/minecraft-server`
- Valheim: `curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com | sh && docker run -d --name valheim -p 2456-2458:2456-2458/udp -v /opt/valheim/config:/config -v /opt/valheim/data:/opt/valheim -e SERVER_NAME='Nxeon' --restart unless-stopped lloesche/valheim-server`

For EACH game find the BEST-MAINTAINED working Docker image (verify on Docker Hub/GitHub 2025-2026; Satisfactory candidate: wolveix/satisfactory-server; Terraria candidates: ryshe/terraria [TShock] or beardedio/terraria). Produce, per game:
1. **Docker image** + why + verified URL.
2. **setupScript** — exact `curl … | sh && docker run -d --name <satisfactory|terraria> … <image>` with correct ports (Satisfactory 7777/udp+tcp, 8888/tcp; Terraria 7777/tcp), volume `-v /opt/<name>:<container path>`, sane env.
3. **Ports to forward**.
4. **game-control**: container name, on-host config file path (Satisfactory: Game.ini/ServerSettings; Terraria: serverconfig.txt or tshock config.json), restart = docker restart.
5. **game-config FamilySchema** TS object literal: `{ family, label, defaultVariant, variants:[{id,label,description}], fields:[{key,label,group,type,default,options?,min?,max?,phase,help?}] }`. Terraria variants = vanilla vs tModLoader vs TShock (pick what the chosen image supports); Satisfactory variants = stable/experimental. ~5 real config fields each (Satisfactory: max players, autosave, advanced game settings toggle; Terraria: difficulty, max players, world size, password).
6. **GamePlan tiers**: `{name, ramMB, cpuCores, diskGB, slots, priceCents}` — Terraria is LIGHT (1-4GB, cheap); Satisfactory scales with factory (8-16GB).
7. **GAME_META**: `{name, tag}`.

Concrete, verify images are real. Write it all as your final message.

# Satisfactory Server Docker Setup

## Docker Run Command

```bash
docker run \
--detach \
--name=satisfactory-server \
--hostname satisfactory-server \
--restart unless-stopped \
--volume ./satisfactory-server:/config \
--env MAXPLAYERS=4 \
--env PGID=1000 \
--env PUID=1000 \
--env STEAMBETA=false \
--memory-reservation=4G \
--memory 8G \
--publish 7777:7777/tcp \
--publish 7777:7777/udp \
--publish 8888:8888/tcp \
wolveix/satisfactory-server:latest
```

## Environment Variables with Defaults

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
|----------|---------|---------|
| MAXPLAYERS | 4 | Player limit |
| PUID | 1000 | User ID |
| PGID | 1000 | Group ID |
| STEAMBETA | false | Experimental version toggle |
| AUTOSAVENUM | 5 | Rotating autosave files |
| DEBUG | false | Debugging mode |
| DISABLESEASONALEVENTS | false | Toggle FICSMAS event |
| LOG | false | Log pruning control |
| MAXOBJECTS | 2162688 | Object limit |
| MAXTICKRATE | 30 | Simulation tick rate |
| SERVERGAMEPORT | 7777 | Game server port |
| SERVERMESSAGINGPORT | 8888 | Messaging port |
| SKIPUPDATE | false | Skip game updates |
| TIMEOUT | 30 | Client timeout (seconds) |

## Ports

- **7777** (TCP/UDP): Game server
- **8888** (TCP): Messaging port

## Volume & Config Paths

- **Host bind path**: `./satisfactory-server` maps to `/config` in container
- **Server settings location**: `/config/saved/` contains blueprints, saves, and server configuration
- **Game files**: `/config/gamefiles/`

## Image Tags

- **Stable**: `wolveix/satisfactory-server:latest`
- **Experimental**: Set `STEAMBETA=true` environment variable

# Terraria Docker Configuration Summary

**Docker Run Command (Existing World):**
```bash
docker run -d --rm -p 7777:7777 -v $HOME/terraria/world:/root/.local/share/Terraria/Worlds --name="terraria" -e WORLD_FILENAME=<.wld> ryshe/terraria:latest
```

**Exposed Ports:**
- 7777 (TCP/UDP for game traffic)
- 7878 (additional port, shown in example output)

**World Volume Path:**
- Host: `$HOME/terraria/world`

content.text:
# Nxeon game-server integration recipes — Satisfactory & Terraria

Both images verified live on Docker Hub / GitHub (checked Aug 2026). Everything below drops straight into the Minecraft/Valheim pattern.

---

## 1. SATISFACTORY

### Docker image
- **Image:** `wolveix/satisfactory-server:latest`
- **Why:** The de-facto community standard for Dockerized Satisfactory. Actively maintained (multiple 2025–2026 releases), handles SteamCMD install/update internally, supports stable + experimental via one env flag, uses a single `/config` volume for saves/settings/gamefiles, and exposes PUID/PGID for clean host permissions.
- **Verified:** https://github.com/wolveix/satisfactory-server and https://hub.docker.com/r/wolveix/satisfactory-server

### setupScript
```bash
curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com | sh && docker run -d --name satisfactory -e MAXPLAYERS=4 -e PUID=1000 -e PGID=1000 -e STEAMBETA=false -e AUTOSAVENUM=5 -e MAXTICKRATE=30 --memory-reservation=4G --memory=8G -p 7777:7777/tcp -p 7777:7777/udp -p 8888:8888/tcp -v /opt/satisfactory:/config --restart unless-stopped wolveix/satisfactory-server:latest
```
(For the experimental variant, flip `-e STEAMBETA=true`.)

### Ports to forward
- `7777/tcp` and `7777/udp` — game traffic
- `8888/tcp` — reliable messaging/API port

### game-control
- **Container name:** `satisfactory`
- **On-host config files:** under the `/opt/satisfactory` bind mount:
  - Server settings/ini: `/opt/satisfactory/gamefiles/FactoryGame/Saved/Config/LinuxServer/Game.ini` and `.../GameUserSettings.ini` (and `ServerSettings` generated after first boot)
  - Saves: `/opt/satisfactory/saved/`
- **Restart:** `docker restart satisfactory`

### game-config FamilySchema
```ts
{
  family: 'satisfactory',
  label: 'Satisfactory',
  defaultVariant: 'stable',
  variants: [
    { id: 'stable', label: 'Stable', description: 'Public stable branch (recommended for most factories)' },
    { id: 'experimental', label: 'Experimental', description: 'Steam beta / experimental branch — newer features, less stable' },
  ],
  fields: [
    { key: 'maxPlayers', label: 'Max Players', group: 'General', type: 'number', default: 4, min: 1, max: 16, phase: 'runtime', help: 'MAXPLAYERS env — concurrent player limit' },
    { key: 'autosaveNum', label: 'Autosave Slots', group: 'World', type: 'number', default: 5, min: 1, max: 20, phase: 'runtime', help: 'AUTOSAVENUM — number of rotating autosave files kept' },
    { key: 'maxTickRate', label: 'Max Tick Rate', group: 'Performance', type: 'number', default: 30, min: 10, max: 60, phase: 'runtime', help: 'MAXTICKRATE — simulation ticks/sec; lower to save CPU on big factories' },
    { key: 'advancedGameSettings', label: 'Advanced Game Settings', group: 'Gameplay', type: 'boolean', default: false, phase: 'runtime', help: 'Enables creative/advanced settings on the save (no achievements)' },
    { key: 'disableSeasonalEvents', label: 'Disable FICSMAS', group: 'Gameplay', type: 'boolean', default: false, phase: 'runtime', help: 'DISABLESEASONALEVENTS — turns off the seasonal event content' },
  ],
}
```

### GamePlan tiers (scales with factory size; RAM-hungry)
```ts
[
  { name: 'Starter Factory',  ramMB: 8192,  cpuCores: 2, diskGB: 20, slots: 4,  priceCents: 1200 },
  { name: 'Industrial',       ramMB: 12288, cpuCores: 4, diskGB: 40, slots: 8,  priceCents: 2000 },
  { name: 'Mega-Factory',     ramMB: 16384, cpuCores: 6, diskGB: 60, slots: 16, priceCents: 3200 },
]
```

### GAME_META
```ts
{ name: 'Satisfactory', tag: 'satisfactory' }
```

---

## 2. TERRARIA

### Docker image
- **Image:** `ryshe/terraria:latest` (TShock-based; pin e.g. `ryshe/terraria:tshock-1.4.5.6-6.1.0` for reproducibility)
- **Why:** Best-maintained Terraria server image — regular tag releases through 2025 tracking both game and TShock versions, auto-loads a `config.json` from the world volume, handles world autocreation, and TShock gives you the admin/REST tooling most hosts want. It also ships plain vanilla tags, so one image covers both variants.
- **Verified:** https://github.com/ryansheehan/terraria and https://hub.docker.com/r/ryshe/terraria

### setupScript
```bash
curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com | sh && docker run -d --name terraria -p 7777:7777/tcp -v /opt/terraria:/root/.local/share/Terraria/Worlds --restart unless-stopped ryshe/terraria:latest -world /root/.local/share/Terraria/Worlds/nxeon.wld -autocreate 2 -difficulty 0 -players 8 -pass ''
```
Notes: `-autocreate` size is `1`=Small `2`=Medium `3`=Large; `-difficulty` `0`=Classic/Normal `1`=Expert `2`=Master `3`=Journey; `-players` = max slots; `-pass` = join password. On first boot the world is generated; thereafter it loads the existing `.wld`. For the pure-vanilla variant, swap `latest` for a vanilla tag (e.g. `ryshe/terraria:1.4.4.9`) — same args, no TShock layer.

### Ports to forward
- `7777/tcp` — game traffic (Terraria is TCP-only)
- (optional) `7878/tcp` — TShock REST API, only if you expose remote admin

### game-control
- **Container name:** `terraria`
- **On-host config files:** under the `/opt/terraria` bind mount:
  - TShock config: `/opt/terraria/config.json` (auto-loaded — this is where password, max slots, MOTD, server name persist for the TShock variant)
  - Vanilla equivalent: a `serverconfig.txt` placed in the same mounted dir and referenced with `-config`
  - World file: `/opt/terraria/nxeon.wld`
- **Restart:** `docker restart terraria`

### game-config FamilySchema
```ts
{
  family: 'terraria',
  label: 'Terraria',
  defaultVariant: 'tshock',
  variants: [
    { id: 'vanilla', label: 'Vanilla', description: 'Stock Terraria dedicated server — closest to single-player rules' },
    { id: 'tshock',  label: 'TShock',  description: 'TShock server with admin commands, permissions & REST API (recommended)' },
  ],
  fields: [
    { key: 'difficulty', label: 'Difficulty', group: 'World', type: 'select', default: '0', options: [
        { value: '0', label: 'Classic / Normal' },
        { value: '1', label: 'Expert' },
        { value: '2', label: 'Master' },
        { value: '3', label: 'Journey' },
      ], phase: 'create', help: '-difficulty — fixed at world creation' },
    { key: 'worldSize', label: 'World Size', group: 'World', type: 'select', default: '2', options: [
        { value: '1', label: 'Small' },
        { value: '2', label: 'Medium' },
        { value: '3', label: 'Large' },
      ], phase: 'create', help: '-autocreate — fixed at world creation' },
    { key: 'maxPlayers', label: 'Max Players', group: 'General', type: 'number', default: 8, min: 1, max: 16, phase: 'runtime', help: '-players / TShock MaxSlots' },
    { key: 'password', label: 'Server Password', group: 'Access', type: 'string', default: '', phase: 'runtime', help: '-pass — blank for open join' },
    { key: 'motd', label: 'MOTD', group: 'General', type: 'string', default: 'Welcome to a Nxeon Terraria server!', phase: 'runtime', help: 'Message of the day shown on join' },
  ],
}
```
(`phase: 'create'` fields — difficulty and worldSize — are baked into the `.wld` at first boot and require a fresh world to change; `runtime` fields apply on restart.)

### GamePlan tiers (Terraria is light and cheap)
```ts
[
  { name: 'Small World', ramMB: 1024, cpuCores: 1, diskGB: 5,  slots: 4,  priceCents: 300 },
  { name: 'Medium',      ramMB: 2048, cpuCores: 1, diskGB: 10, slots: 8,  priceCents: 500 },
  { name: 'Large',       ramMB: 4096, cpuCores: 2, diskGB: 15, slots: 16, priceCents: 800 },
]
```

### GAME_META
```ts
{ name: 'Terraria', tag: 'terraria' }
```

---

### Integration notes / caveats
- **Satisfactory RAM:** the image sets `--memory 8G` as a floor; large factories genuinely need 12–16 GB, so the tiers above lead with 8 GB — don't undersell it. Ports 7777 (tcp+udp) AND 8888/tcp both required or clients can't join.
- **Terraria world-creation fields** (difficulty, size) are permanent for a given `.wld` — surface them as create-time-only in the UI so users don't expect a restart to change them.
- **Pin tags in production:** `latest` on both images moves; capturing the current tag (`wolveix/satisfactory-server:latest` digest, `ryshe/terraria:tshock-1.4.5.6-6.1.0`) in the plan record avoids surprise breakage on redeploy.
- Both follow the exact `curl … | sh && docker run -d --name <name> … <image>` shape and use a single `/opt/<name>` host volume, so they slot into the existing game-control (name + config path + `docker restart`) abstraction with no special-casing.

Sources: [wolveix/satisfactory-server GitHub](https://github.com/wolveix/satisfactory-server) · [wolveix Docker Hub](https://hub.docker.com/r/wolveix/satisfactory-server) · [ryansheehan/terraria GitHub](https://github.com/ryansheehan/terraria) · [ryshe/terraria Docker Hub](https://hub.docker.com/r/ryshe/terraria)
